```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: !expr has_data
# Every data-dependent sentence is built here from `results`, with a branch
# for each way the data could fall.
p <- results$primary
pa <- results$per_assessment
later <- pa[-1, ]
b <- results$bounds
ab <- results$absent_bound
adj <- results$adjusted

s_primary <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "Thirty minutes after arrival in the recovery room, %s patients who gargled",
    "sugar water had a sore throat at rest, against %s who gargled licorice: a",
    "risk difference of %s. The marginal odds ratio is %s (%s)."
  ),
  fmt_prop(p$p_sugar, p$n_sugar), fmt_prop(p$p_licorice, p$n_licorice),
  fmt_rd(p), fmt_or(p), fmt_p(p$p_value)
)
s_answer_1 <- if (p$upper < 1) {
  "**Yes.** Licorice reduced sore throat in the recovery room."
} else if (p$lower > 1) {
  "**No.** Sore throat was more common after licorice."
} else {
  "**Not shown.** The data cannot rule out no effect."
}
s_robust <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "Adjusting for baseline covariates gives a conditional odds ratio of %s.",
    "Filling in the missing outcomes of patients in the file in the way least",
    "favourable to licorice gives %s.%s"
  ),
  fmt_or(adj), fmt_or(b[2, ]),
  if (ab$n_absent > 0) {
    sprintf(
      paste(
        " Also counting the %d enrolled %s absent from the file as a licorice",
        "patient with a sore throat (post hoc) gives %s."
      ),
      ab$n_absent, if (ab$n_absent == 1) "patient" else "patients", fmt_or(ab)
    )
  } else {
    ""
  }
)
s_robust_verdict <- if (all(c(adj$upper, b$upper, ab$upper) < 1)) {
  "None of these checks moves the confidence interval to include one."
} else {
  "At least one of these checks gives a confidence interval that includes one (Chapters 2 and 6)."
}

or_below <- all(pa$upper < 1)
rd_below <- all(pa$rd_upper < 0)
s_answer_2 <- if (or_below && rd_below) {
  "**The data are consistent with a benefit that lasts past the recovery room.**"
} else {
  "**The data do not show a benefit at every later assessment.**"
}
s_durability <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "The marginal odds ratio is %s at ninety minutes, %s at four hours and %s on",
    "the first postoperative morning, when the risk difference is %s."
  ),
  fmt_or(later[1, ]), fmt_or(later[2, ]), fmt_or(later[3, ]), fmt_rd(later[3, ])
)
s_durability_verdict <- if (or_below && rd_below) {
  paste(
    "At every assessment the confidence interval for the odds ratio lies below one",
    "and the interval for the risk difference below zero. These are descriptive",
    "estimates with no formal test across time and no multiplicity adjustment",
    "(D-003, D-013)."
  )
} else {
  paste(
    "At least one later assessment has an interval that includes no effect. That",
    "does not show the effect wore off, only that the data cannot rule out no",
    "effect there (D-013)."
  )
}
s_common <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "Summarising all four assessments in one number, which assumes a common effect",
    "and does not itself answer this question, the population-averaged (marginal)",
    "odds ratio is %s. The patient-level (conditional) odds ratio from the mixed",
    "model is %s.%s"
  ),
  fmt_or(results$gee), fmt_or(results$glmm),
  if (abs(results$glmm$log_or) > abs(results$gee$log_or)) {
    paste(
      " It is further from one because it compares the same patient under each",
      "gargle, not because the effect is larger (D-008)."
    )
  } else {
    " Unusually, it is no further from one than the marginal estimate (Chapter 7)."
  }
)
s_enrolled <- if (ab$n_absent > 0) {
  sprintf(
    paste(
      "**Enrolled but not in the file.** The codebook counts %d enrolled; the file",
      "has %d. Why is not yet known."
    ),
    results$n_enrolled, results$n_patients
  )
} else {
  "**Enrollment.** The file holds every enrolled patient."
}
s_no_postop <- sprintf(
  paste(
    "**No post-operative data.** %d patients in the file have no post-operative",
    "data. Why is not yet known; they are in the bounds above."
  ),
  results$no_postop_n
)
```

## The questions

The PI asked, at the intake meeting (Chapter 1):

> "did it reduce sore throat afterwards?"

> "does it last past the recovery room?"

Every comparison is licorice against sugar water, among patients
randomized to them, with any sore throat at rest (a score above zero on the
zero-to-ten scale) as the outcome.

## Did it reduce sore throat?

`r if (has_data) s_answer_1 else "*Awaiting results.*"`
`r if (has_data) s_primary else ""`

`r if (has_data) s_robust else ""`
`r if (has_data) s_robust_verdict else ""`
Details are in Chapter 6, with the bounds in Chapter 2.

## Does it last past the recovery room?

`r if (has_data) s_answer_2 else "*Awaiting results.*"`
`r if (has_data) s_durability else ""`
`r if (has_data) s_durability_verdict else ""`

`r if (has_data) s_common else ""`
Details are in Chapter 7.

## What is still open

These questions for the client could not be answered from the data
(Chapter 1).

- `r if (has_data) s_enrolled else "**Enrollment.** To be checked when data arrive."`
  If a randomized patient is missing, the analysis is not fully intention
  to treat.
- `r if (has_data) s_no_postop else "**No post-operative data.** To be checked when data arrive."`
- **Swallowing pain.** Not analysed. The PI was undecided. Adding it now,
  after the results have been seen, would be a post hoc analysis and would
  be reported as one.
- **Stratified randomization.** Not yet known. If randomization was
  stratified, the unadjusted analysis gives conservative standard errors.
- **Preoperative sore throat in the protocol.** Whether the protocol
  excluded these patients is not yet known. The analysis keeps them
  (D-005).

## How to read this book

It is both the lab notebook and the report. The *Plan* part was written
before the results. Additions made after it was locked are marked as such,
and the one made after results were seen is labeled post hoc. The
*Results* part follows it, and the *Record* part holds every analysis
decision and the research log. Every number in the Plan, Results and
Summary prose is computed from the data when the book renders, so the
text cannot drift from the analysis; `make numbers` checks this. The
decision record and research log are hand-written logs, and say so.
